title: FLORA STUDENTS EXCEL
full_story:
Flora High School students, Sydney Dawkins, Kristen Pipher, Paul Hudson, Qynlin Brown, Hayden Young, Ella Cammon, Justice Scroggins, Kinley Atwood, and Meredith Woolever placed among the top students in Illinois in the 2026 Office Specialist (MOS) State Championship for Spring Semester.

The MOS State Championship consists of six certification exams covering Microsoft Office products such as Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.  Sydney Dawkins placed 4th in Excel and 2nd in Word with a perfect score; Kristen Pipher placed 2nd in Excel with a perfect score; Meredith Woolever placed 3rd in PowerPoint with a perfect score; Paul Hudson placed 1st in Excel with a perfect score, Qynlin Brown placed 8th in Excel, Justice Scroggins placed 9th in Excel, Hayden Young placed 1st in PowerPoint with a perfect score, Ella Cammon 4th place in PowerPoint with a perfect score, and Kinley Atwood 7th place in Excel.

1st place winners earn the opportunity to attend the Microsoft National Competition in Nashville, Tennessee in June.  Out of six available slots, Flora placed first in four.

Students attending the National competition compete against other students from 50 states for scholarships.  Paul Hudson will be competing in Excel, Kristen Pipher in PowerPoint, Hayden Young in PowerPoint, and Payton Scroggins in Word; the competition will be in Nashville in June.  Students are currently seeking donations to help with the travel costs.

These MOS exams are industry-standard assessments and to finish this high in the state proves to potential employers that you have mastered the skills.  Flora High School has been a Microsoft testing facility for six years.

title: EFFINGHAM STABBING
full_story:
At approximately 11:30 pm Monday, Effingham Police Department received reports of a stabbing in the 500 block of North Henrietta Street.

Officers located a victim with an apparent stab wound to the torso who was transported to St. Anthony’s Hospital.  Witnesses stated the suspect fled the scene prior to the officers’ arrival.  Based on the initial investigation, officers identified the suspect as Samuel J. Sarver, 20, of Effingham.  Officers located Sarver a brief time later and he was taken into custody without further incident.  Sarver was transported to the Effingham County Jail.  The victim was transferred to Carle Foundation Hospital in Urbana.

An initial court appearance was held Wednesday and Sarver was charged with Aggravated Battery with a Deadly Weapon, Reckless Conduct with Great Bodily Harm both Class 3 Felonies; and Unlawful Use of a Weapon a Class A Misdemeanor.  Judge Wesley Gozia ordered Sarver detained pending trial.

title: FOWLER TO RESIGN
full_story:
State Senator Dale Fowler announced that he will be resigning.

Fowler will resign following the conclusion of the 2026 legislative session, ending nearly a decade representing the 59th Senate District in Southern Illinois.

Fowler says the decision follows a commitment to serve no more than 10 years and to opt out of a legislative pension.  He was first elected in 2016 and began serving in 2017.

Accomplishments include projects such as helping bring Walker’s Bluff Casino Resort to Southern Illinois, the SI Treasures tourism initiative, creation of the Southern Illinois Made Expo, and much more.

Republican leaders from counties within the 59th Senate District will select someone to temporarily fill the vacancy until the next election.

title: USDA WAIVER
full_story:
The US Department of Transportation and USDA announced the administration is temporarily waiving hours-of-service rules for fertilizer deliveries to help get critical supply to farmers faster.

Federal regulations limit the hours of service a driver may operate a commercial motor vehicle transporting property in interstate commerce.  In response to a request from The Fertilizer Institute (TFI), the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration issued a waiver Tuesday loosening driving time restrictions for haulers carrying straight or blended fertilizer products in 35 states, including Illinois.

Under the waiver, fertilizer haulers could drive 16 hours within a 24-hour period and must take at least one six-hour break in a sleeper berth every 24 hours, or one eight-hour break if they don’t have a sleeper berth.

Normal hours-of-service rules don’t allow truckers to begin a driving shift until they have spent 10 consecutive hours off duty, and they must rest again after 14 consecutive hours of driving.

The release noted it is not uncommon for agricultural states to have seasonal waivers for hours of service around peak planting or harvesting times.  Waiving such regulations for fertilizer deliveries was a potential policy solution TFI shared with the White House in a letter earlier this month.

title: UTZ RECALL
full_story:
Utz is recalling two of its popular potato chip brands due to the risk of salmonella contamination.  The company is recalling select flavors and bag sizes of Zapp’s and Dirty brand potato chips because the company was notified that the milk powder in some of its seasonings may contain salmonella and had been recalled separately.

Utz is voluntarily recalling these chips out of an abundance of caution although tested seasonings were negative for the bacteria.  No illnesses have been reported in connection with the recalled chips, but the company advises against consuming the products.

Salmonella is an organism which can cause serious and sometimes fatal infections in young children, frail or elderly people, and others with weakened immune systems.  Healthy persons infected with Salmonella often experience fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting and abdominal pain.  In rare circumstances, infection with Salmonella can result in the organism getting into the bloodstream and producing more severe illnesses such as arterial infections, endocarditis and arthritis.

To date, there have been no complaints of illness reported to Utz in connection with the recalled products.  Utz is recalling these products based on the ingredient supplier’s recall.

Consumers who have these products should not eat them and should discard any products they may have.  For questions or refunds, consumers may contact the Utz Customer Care team email or call 1-877-423-0149, Monday through Friday from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm Eastern Time.  Retailers should check their inventories and shelves to confirm that none of the products are present or available for purchase by consumers.  This voluntary recall is being conducted with the knowledge of the United States Food and Drug Administration.

title: NEW DISPLAY AT LINCOLN LIBRARY
full_story:
America’s Civil War ended slavery and offered African Americans new status as full citizens with the right to vote and hold office.  It was, in many ways, a second founding of the American republic.  But as visitors to the Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum will see in a new exhibit, these rights were soon stripped away in a barrage of violence, political deals and hostile court rulings.

“The Second American Revolution,” opening at the museum June 5th, will trace the efforts to rebuild America to match Lincoln’s vision and then document the backlash that gave rise to Jim Crow laws and decades of oppression.

The exhibit, part of the ALPLM’s commemoration of America’s 250th birthday, includes historic pieces such as the pen Lincoln used to sign the Emancipation Proclamation, a copy of the constitutional amendment ending slavery, Ku Klux Klan paraphernalia and a chair from Ford’s Theatre, where Lincoln was assassinated.

The exhibit also includes short films about refugee camps for people escaping slavery during the Civil War, an interactive collection of short biographies of women who worked to end slavery, a short film about the 13th, 14th and 15th amendments and a timeline of efforts to reverse Reconstruction.

The exhibit was curated by Manisha Sinha, author of “The Rise and Fall of the Second American Republic: Reconstruction, 1860-1920” and “The Slave’s Cause: A History of Abolition.”  She is also the James L. and Shirley A. Draper Chair in American History at the University of Connecticut and past president of the Society for Historians of the Early American Republic.

For more information, visit www.PresidentLincoln.illinois.gov.  You can follow the ALPLM on Facebook, X/Twitter and Instagram.
